rows: Decode one vector tile (.mvt/.pbf file or URL) into one row per feature

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a single Mapbox Vector Tile into one row per feature. Positional arguments: `source` (a .mvt/.pbf URL, or a local path under Bun; gzip is detected) and the tile's `z`, `x`, `y` (XYZ scheme), which place its pixels on the map. Named arguments: `layer` and `coordinates` as in read_tiles. Returns the same columns as read_tiles; the tile is returned as stored, including its buffer.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## read_mvt(source, z, x, y, layer := NULL, coordinates := 'wgs84')

Decode one vector tile. The `z/x/y` address is needed to turn tile pixels into coordinates.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Features per geometry type in the fixture tile","sql":"SELECT geometry_type, count(*) AS n FROM mvt.main.read_mvt('test/fixtures/0-0-0.mvt', 0, 0, 0) GROUP BY geometry_type ORDER BY geometry_type"},{"description":"For each attribute the sample tileset's metadata declares (tileset_layers), how many of the standalone tile 0/0/0's features in that layer carry a value for it (read_mvt)","sql":"SELECT t.layer, t.field, count(f.layer) AS features, count(f.properties->>t.field) AS with_value FROM mvt.main.tileset_layers('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') AS t LEFT JOIN mvt.main.read_mvt('test/fixtures/0-0-0.mvt', 0, 0, 0) AS f ON f.layer = t.layer GROUP BY t.layer, t.field ORDER BY t.layer, t.field"}]

Read the vector tiles of a PMTiles archive or XYZ tile server at one zoom as one row per feature

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Read every vector tile of a tileset at one zoom level and return one row per feature: layer, z, x, y, feature_id, geometry_type, geometry (GEOMETRY, WGS84 by default), properties (JSON). `source` is a PMTiles archive (http(s) URL read with range requests, or a local path under Bun) or a tile URL template with {z}/{x}/{y}. Named arguments: `zoom` (default: the tileset's maxzoom), `layer` (one layer, adding a typed column per attribute the metadata lists), `west`/`south`/`east`/`north` (a WGS84 bbox that selects tiles; required for URL templates), `coordinates` ('wgs84', 'web_mercator' or 'tile'), `tile_edges` ('merge', the default, joins a feature's pieces across tiles into one row; 'clip' trims pieces to their tile; 'raw' returns tiles as stored) and `max_tiles` (default 10000). A bbox argument selects tiles, not features. `WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, <constant geometry>)` (or ST_Contains, ST_Within, ST_Covers, ST_Overlaps, ...) is pushed down: its bounding box chooses the tiles, and DuckDB still applies the exact predicate. The box must be a constant: one from a join, an OR or a NOT isn't pushed.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## read_tiles(source, zoom := maxzoom, layer := NULL, west/south/east/north := NULL, coordinates := 'wgs84', tile_edges := 'merge', max_tiles := 10000)

Read a PMTiles archive or XYZ tile server at one zoom as one row per feature. Remote PMTiles are read with HTTP range requests, so a bbox over a planet-sized archive fetches only the directory pages and tiles under it.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Count the fixture tileset's features per layer at zoom 2","sql":"SELECT layer, count(*) AS features FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', zoom := 2) GROUP BY layer ORDER BY layer"},{"description":"Road kinds in central Florence from the Protomaps sample, over HTTP range requests","sql":"SELECT \"pmap:kind\" AS kind, count(*) AS n FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/protomaps/PMTiles/main/spec/v3/protomaps(vector)ODbL_firenze.pmtiles', layer := 'roads', west := 11.24, south := 43.76, east := 11.27, north := 43.78) GROUP BY kind ORDER BY n DESC"},{"description":"Spatial join of two layers: the region polygon (if any) each city of the fixture tileset lies in, using the typed columns layer := adds","sql":"SELECT c.name, c.population, r.code AS region, r.label FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'cities') AS c LEFT JOIN mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'regions') AS r ON ST_Within(c.geometry, r.geometry) ORDER BY c.name"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description":"Count the fixture tileset's features per layer at zoom 2","sql":"SELECT layer, count(*) AS features FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', zoom := 2) GROUP BY layer ORDER BY layer","expected_result":[["cities",4],["regions",2]]},{"description":"Spatial join of two layers: the region polygon (if any) each city of the fixture tileset lies in, using the typed columns layer := adds","sql":"SELECT c.name, c.population, r.code AS region, r.label FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'cities') AS c LEFT JOIN mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'regions') AS r ON ST_Within(c.geometry, r.geometry) ORDER BY c.name","expected_result":[["Berlin",3645000,null,null],["Milan",1352000,"A","Square with a hole"],["Paris",2148000,null,null],["Vienna",1897000,null,null]]}]

List a tileset's layers and their attributes from its vector_layers metadata

rows.vgi.doc_llm: List the layers of a PMTiles tileset and their attributes, from the archive's TileJSON `vector_layers` metadata: one row per (layer, attribute) with the attribute type (String, Number, Boolean), plus each layer's zoom range and description. Use it before read_tiles to learn layer names and which typed columns `layer := '<name>'` will add.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## tileset_layers(source)

One row per layer attribute, from the tileset's `vector_layers` metadata.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Attributes of the fixture tileset's cities layer","sql":"SELECT field, type FROM mvt.main.tileset_layers('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') WHERE layer = 'cities' ORDER BY field"},{"description":"Profile the fixture tileset: each layer's declared attributes and zoom range (tileset_layers) beside its feature count and geometry types at the max zoom (read_tiles)","sql":"WITH declared AS (SELECT layer, string_agg(field, ', ' ORDER BY field) AS attributes, min(minzoom) AS minzoom, max(maxzoom) AS maxzoom FROM mvt.main.tileset_layers('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') GROUP BY layer), found AS (SELECT layer, count(*) AS features, string_agg(DISTINCT geometry_type, ', ') AS geometry_types FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') GROUP BY layer) SELECT d.layer, d.attributes, d.minzoom, d.maxzoom, f.features, f.geometry_types FROM declared AS d LEFT JOIN found AS f USING (layer) ORDER BY d.layer"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description":"Attributes of the fixture tileset's cities layer","sql":"SELECT field, type FROM mvt.main.tileset_layers('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') WHERE layer = 'cities' ORDER BY field","expected_result":[["capital","Boolean"],["name","String"],["population","Number"]]},{"description":"Profile the fixture tileset: each layer's declared attributes and zoom range (tileset_layers) beside its feature count and geometry types at the max zoom (read_tiles)","sql":"WITH declared AS (SELECT layer, string_agg(field, ', ' ORDER BY field) AS attributes, min(minzoom) AS minzoom, max(maxzoom) AS maxzoom FROM mvt.main.tileset_layers('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') GROUP BY layer), found AS (SELECT layer, count(*) AS features, string_agg(DISTINCT geometry_type, ', ') AS geometry_types FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') GROUP BY layer) SELECT d.layer, d.attributes, d.minzoom, d.maxzoom, f.features, f.geometry_types FROM declared AS d LEFT JOIN found AS f USING (layer) ORDER BY d.layer","expected_result":[["cities","capital, name, population",0,3,4,"POINT"],["regions","area_rank, code, label",0,3,2,"POLYGON"]]}]
